A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dynamic Negative Guidance work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations, MNIST and CIFAR10 class-removal experiments, and Stable Diffusion evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of further removal targets, trajectory examples and quantitative text-to-image summaries.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same posterior-weighted guidance, Markov-chain posterior estimation, temperature, offset and clamping. The Stable Diffusion adaptation was already present in v1; the revision introduces no new generation procedure.

E1.justification: Class-removal coverage expands from MNIST zero and CIFAR10 airplanes to digits 0–3 and airplanes, cars, birds and cats (v2 Figures 4 and 14). This extends target coverage within the existing datasets and task; the five-prompt quantitative text-to-image study remains.

E2.justification: Class removal continues to compare against Negative Prompting and Safe Latent Diffusion. Text-to-image comparisons retain Negative Prompting, and Gaussian examples retain CFG, NP and unguided controls.

E3.justification: Appendix H adds the Q evaluation metric and its regression-based aggregation. Reported guidance settings also change: the dinner-table example lists DNG scale 27 in v1 Figure 14 but 12 in v2 Figure 17, without establishing a rerun. The principal 10,240-image class-removal and 32-image text-to-image protocols remain.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 11 supplies sensitivity curves for the previously described SLD threshold search. Figure 5 adds two trajectory-level text-to-image case studies illustrating guidance timing and image changes. Earlier average-guidance analyses and guidance-strength sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: Table 4 introduces aggregate Q values with ± terms, but does not define the uncertainty measure or its repeated-run basis. This adds statistical reporting without establishing additional runs; averaging text-to-image results over 32 images was already documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds six class-target result sets and five Q comparisons; Table 4 reports, for example, Prompt 1 scores of -0.015 for NP and 0.053 for DNG. The original zero-removal and airplane-removal curves are preserved. Figure 6's numerical CLIP results also change, without an explanation establishing why.

T1.justification: v2 corrects summation indexing in Equation 11 and the variance index in Equation 13. Appendix H adds the mathematical definition of Q and its linear-regression derivation in Equations 23–24. The central DNG derivation and Appendix B–C proof material remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal claims: training-free dynamic guidance, improved class-removal tradeoffs, and less invasive text-to-image guidance. Expanded experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning NP's dependence on the removal target, guidance timing and SLD threshold extremes. Section 4.2 also acknowledges that images altered by unrelated NP can still satisfy the positive prompt. The main limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract supplies an implementation repository link, whereas v1 only promises release upon acceptance; that older promise remains in v2's introduction. Appendix D.3 expands documentation of ChatGPT-suggested related objects and manual prompt checks. Tables 1–3 retain their settings.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds two negative-prompting blog references, Andrew (2023) and Bhasin (2024), and more explicit discussion of Ban et al.'s timing observations and Armandpour et al.'s orthogonal guidance. The central positioning against NP and SLD remains.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify guidance terminology and text-to-image evaluation, reorganize Section 2.3, and separate class-removal material into Appendix G while moving the text-to-image appendix to H. The overall narrative and much of the prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: Figure 1 becomes a single row, class-removal displays expand to four targets, and MNIST plots move to the appendix. New trajectory and sensitivity figures and Table 4 are added. Figure 6's axes change, and appendix image grids shrink from sixteen examples to four larger examples with expanded captions.

improvement.justification: Testing four removal targets per dataset reduces dependence on v1's single-target evidence, and Figure 11 makes SLD threshold selection more inspectable. These benefits are limited by unchanged text-to-image validation gaps and reporting problems: Table 4 leaves its ± terms undefined and reports an NP average of 0.007 although its five entries average 0.0124.
